newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD sees half point U.S. rate rise to stem growth.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees half point U.S. rate rise to stem growth.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said in its half-yearly Economic Outlook on Thursday that it expected a half-point rate rise in the U.S. to slow growth.

"In its projections, the OECD Secretariat is assuming another 0.5 percentage point rise in the federal funds rate around the middle of 1997, which may be needed to slow economic growth to a sustainable pace and push unemployment back up towards its structural rate," the rich-nation's economic think-tank said in its report.

The OECD said that along with this further tightening, long-term interest rates were projected to peak in the latter half of 1997 before edging back down as the need for further policy restaints waned.

The OECD said that the trade-weighted value of the dollar had appreciated significantly from end 1996 to May 1997 after having been relatively flat until the middle of 1996. "The dollar's appreciation should help contain inflation somewhat but also lead to further deterioration in net exports over the projection period despite reversing relative cyclical positions between the United States and its trading partners," it said.
